function: SAC reinforcement learning predicts mobile-user positions for CSI; a dual-layer deep-unfolding network sets the transmit beamformer and UAV position to maximize sum-rate (p. 3, 9).
system: UAV with 3x3 planar array (M = 9), K = 3 single-antenna mobile ground users, LoS channel, 50 m altitude; frequency band not stated (p. 4, 10).
method: SAC deep reinforcement learning for tracking; deep unfolding of WMMSE and projected gradient with trainable step sizes and offsets, trained unsupervised on the sum-rate loss (p. 6, 9).
data_channel: Own LoS channel (-60 dB reference gain, array response); user motion from public ETH pedestrian trajectories, 30 time slots (p. 4, 10).
test_conditions: Train and test on filtered ETH trajectories (30 slots); network trained at Pmax = 30 dBm also tested at 10, 20 and 40 dBm (p. 10, 13).
baselines: Tracking: learned LSTM and RNN. Beamforming: non-learned WMMSE. Trajectory: non-learned PSO, SCA, fixed route and fixed position (p. 11, 12).
metrics: Prediction error (m), sum-rate (bits/s/Hz), percentage of the WMMSE upper bound, GPU training time (p. 11-13).
complexity: DUN O(Nv K M^2) versus WMMSE O(Lo K M^3) (p. 10); GPU training time per number of layers in Table III (p. 12).
q1_support: p. 4: "we focus solely on the LoS components"; the channel is the paper's own LoS model with array response. The ETH data (p. 10) gives only pedestrian positions; no 3GPP model, public ray-tracing set or measured channel is used.
q2_support: p. 13: "we train the network under Pmax = 30 dBm and test it under different values of maximum transmission power"; a power-budget (SNR) sweep, which the criterion excludes. Position-noise tests (p. 11) are error sweeps; no new scenario, K, M or dataset.
q3_support: p. 11: "we train LSTM and RNN networks as benchmark algorithms" (tracking error); p. 12: "the DUN performance reaches 98.5% of the WMMSE performance upper bound after convergence"; p. 13: PSO and SCA compared on sum-rate.
q4_support: p. 10: "The computational complexity of the proposed DUN can be expressed as O(Nv KM 2 )", against O(Lo KM 3 ) for WMMSE; Table III (p. 12) lists GPU training time.
q5_support: p. 10: "All experiments are performed on the publicly available pedestrian trajectory: ETH [39] dataset"; these are user-motion data for the tracker, not channels or signals, the channel is simulated, and no code or data link is given.
notes: Area 6 by the precedence rule (UAV aerial link, beams and trajectory); the radar (ISAC) only gives initial user positions (p. 4, 5), so area 5 also fits. Reviewer to confirm: q2 (Table IV, train at 30 dBm and test at other power budgets, treated as an SNR sweep) and q1 and q5 (ETH trajectories are public and measured but are user-motion data for the tracker, not channels or signals; the channel is simulated). q3 split: LSTM and RNN for the tracker, WMMSE, PSO and SCA for the unfolding network.
